extra_quotes: Our developed prototype extends NEORV32 v1.12.8.3 on a Digilent Nexys A7-100T board with a Xilinx Artix-7 XC7A100T FPGA.
Latency is measured with a Vivado Integrated Logic Analyzer (ILA), whereas resource, timing, and full-system power results come from separate non-instrumented post-implementation builds.
The prototype leaves NEORV32’s DMA controller disabled, requiring software to copy each protected packet from the wrapper to data memory and then load it into the CFU.
In the prototype, the key is fixed in the FPGA configuration; a deployment would protect it with bitstream encryption or derive the key from a PUF [15], and would need per-device key provisioning.
Lastly, the prototype holds one four-byte accelerometer packet at a time.
